About

I'm a Service Designer turned UX/Product Designer with a Master's in Service Design from SCAD and 3+ years translating complex user needs, organizational structures, and system logic into intuitive interfaces, service blueprints, and measurable product outcomes.

App Orchid · Oct 2024 – Present · Remote Partnered with 6+ enterprise clients to translate their needs into AI-driven tool workflows and backend logic. Questions, questions, questions.

The stuff people usually wonder about before reaching out — AI included.

You could design with AI, and I could design with AI — but the results would look nothing alike. I spent 6 years studying the fundamentals of design, so I use AI as a tool, not a master. Left on its own, AI tends to average out every design it's seen. With real design fundamentals behind it, you get something better than average.

I use AI to quickly generate mockups of my ideas. Not every idea makes the cut, so it's not worth spending an hour hand-crafting each one — AI lets me explore more directions fast, then invest real time into the ones that are actually worth pursuing.

I bring creativity only a human mind can offer — connecting uncommon dots that AI, trained on existing patterns, simply won't reach.

I'm looking for a full-time role, though I'm open to starting with a short internship of a few months if that's a better fit for how a team wants to bring me on.

Every project has its own process, but here's roughly how it goes in my current product development role: I get a brief from the project manager, and I ask a lot of questions upfront to really understand the reasoning behind the request — not just the ask itself. From there, I move into Figma and build using our design system, always creating a few options rather than one — it's much easier to compare and decide than to sit with a single design and try to pinpoint what's not working. Then we have a review call, and based on feedback I either iterate or hand it off to engineering for development.

Working at a startup means wearing multiple hats — my work spans UI/UX design, QA, research, business problem-solving, and sometimes even a bit of coding.

It depends on scope — small briefs can be turned around in a day, while larger projects run 2–3 months depending on the requirements.

Figma — from early wireframes to polished, developer-ready screens.
